svg.font-family: 'Roboto Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
svg.title: How E2B spawns a sandbox
svg.desc: At template build time E2B boots the template, snapshots it, records which guest pages fault in, and stores a snapfile, a layered memfile, a layered rootfs, and metadata. Every spawn then resumes that snapshot, so the orchestrator starts Firecracker in a network namespace without the jailer, loads the snapshot with a userfaultfd backend, serves guest memory page by page from the memfile layers, prefaults the recorded hot pages, serves the rootfs over NBD, resumes the VM, puts only a SHA-512 hash of the access token into MMDS, and then posts the real token to envd inside the guest, which checks it against the hash. The token is never in the snapshot files on disk, but it is in guest RAM once envd holds it.
svg.text: Every spawn is a snapshot resume
No warm pool. Each sandbox is a paused microVM, brought back from its template.
once, when the template is built
Firecracker in a netns, no jailer
userfaultfd serves RAM, hot pages first
MMDS gets the hash, not the token
envd checks the token after resume
the token is not in the snapshot. it is in guest RAM once envd holds it.
